sydney-opera-house.blurb: The sails are covered in more than a million Swedish-made tiles that clean themselves when it rains. Utzon's winning entry was little more than a set of sketches.

eiffel-tower.blurb: Leading Parisian artists protested against this 'useless and monstrous' tower before it went up. It's repainted by hand roughly every seven years and grows about 15 cm on hot days as the iron expands.

burj-khalifa.blurb: At 828 m it's so tall you can watch the sun set at the base, take the lift up, and watch it set again. The spire alone is taller than many skyscrapers.

colosseum.blurb: Under the arena floor ran a maze of tunnels and lifts that hoisted animals and scenery up through trapdoors. After Rome fell it served as a quarry, a fortress and even housing.

taj-mahal.blurb: Some 20,000 workers are said to have spent over two decades on the complex. The white marble changes colour through the day, from pinkish at dawn to milky white at noon.

empire-state-building.blurb: It rose at an astonishing four and a half storeys a week. It has its own ZIP code, and lightning hits it about 20 times a year.

sagrada-familia.blurb: Asked why it was taking so long, Gaudí reportedly replied that his client was not in a hurry. Inside, the columns branch like trees into a stone forest.

st-basils.blurb: Legend says Ivan the Terrible blinded the architects so they could never build anything as beautiful again (almost certainly untrue). The famous colours were added long after it was built.

petronas-towers.blurb: From 1998 to 2004 they were the tallest buildings in the world. The skybridge isn't fixed rigidly to the towers, so it can slide as they sway.

leaning-tower-pisa.blurb: It began to lean while still being built, so the upper floors were made slightly taller on one side to compensate. Engineers spent 1990–2001 straightening it by about 40 cm.

parthenon.blurb: It stood largely intact for 2,000 years until 1687, when a Venetian cannonball hit gunpowder stored inside. Many of its sculptures now live in the British Museum.

big-ben.blurb: The great bell cracked soon after it was hung and still rings slightly out of tune. Old pennies placed on the pendulum fine-tune the clock's timekeeping.

forbidden-city.blurb: Legend says it has 9,999 rooms, one short of heaven's 10,000. Off-limits for nearly 500 years, it's now one of the most visited places on Earth.

notre-dame.blurb: Victor Hugo's novel about its hunchbacked bell-ringer helped save it from ruin in the 1800s. After the 2019 fire, it reopened in December 2024.

pantheon.blurb: It has been in use for almost 2,000 years, today as a church. When it rains, the water falls through the open eye and drains away through small holes in the floor.

cn-tower.blurb: Thrill-seekers can walk around the outside of the main pod, strapped to a rail 356 m up. It's struck by lightning dozens of times a year.

hagia-sophia.blurb: For nearly a thousand years it was the largest cathedral in the world. Its first dome collapsed after an earthquake in 558 and was rebuilt taller.

marina-bay-sands.blurb: The rooftop pool is about 150 m long and sits some 200 m above the bay. The deck overhangs the north tower by about 65 m.

guggenheim-bilbao.blurb: Gehry's team designed its curves with CATIA, software made for designing fighter jets. The titanium skin is less than half a millimetre thick and ripples like fish scales.

neuschwanstein.blurb: Ludwig II paid for it from his own fortune, not the state's. It opened to paying visitors weeks after his mysterious death, and it inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

fallingwater.blurb: The Kaufmann family expected a house with a view of their favourite waterfall; Wright put them right on top of it. The cantilevers sagged for decades until they were reinforced in 2002.

villa-savoye.blurb: The roof leaked so badly that the Savoye family complained bitterly for years. Today it's one of the most influential houses of the 20th century.

chrysler-building.blurb: Its gargoyles are steel eagle heads and radiator caps modelled on Chrysler cars. It was the world's tallest building for less than a year.

lotus-temple.blurb: It has no altar, no clergy and no sermons, yet it ranks among the most visited buildings in the world. Nine pools around it help keep the hall cool.

sheikh-zayed-mosque.blurb: Its main chandelier is one of the largest in the world. The carpet in the main prayer hall was hand-knotted by about 1,200 artisans.

atomium.blurb: It was built to stand for six months and never came down. The top sphere holds a restaurant with a view over all of Brussels.

alhambra.blurb: Its name means 'the red one', after the colour of its walls. Inside, the walls are covered in Arabic poetry carved into the stucco.

potala-palace.blurb: It has more than 1,000 rooms and sits about 3,700 m above sea level, so many visitors are out of breath before they reach the top.

angkor-wat.blurb: Its sandstone blocks came from quarries tens of kilometres away, probably by canal. It's the centrepiece of Cambodia's national flag.

cctv-hq.blurb: The loop's overhanging corner juts out about 75 m in mid-air. The irregular grid on the facade is densest where the structure works hardest.

oslo-opera-house.blurb: Locals picnic, sunbathe and skateboard on its roof. The marble was quarried in Carrara, Italy.

elbphilharmonie.blurb: A curved escalator 82 m long carries you up through the old warehouse. Costs grew to about ten times the original budget, and Hamburg got a world-class concert hall.

brasilia-cathedral.blurb: Most of the church sits below ground: you enter through a dark passage and emerge into a bright glass hall. Four bronze evangelists guard the entrance.

taipei-101.blurb: The giant damper ball is so popular it has its own cartoon mascots, the 'Damper Babies'. Its lifts were once the fastest in the world.

habitat-67.blurb: Safdie wanted to give apartment dwellers a garden, so each unit's terrace is the roof of the one below. He still keeps an apartment there.

kunsthaus-graz.blurb: At night its skin becomes a giant low-resolution screen made of 930 fluorescent rings. The nickname stuck so well that the museum uses it too.

heydar-aliyev-center.blurb: There are almost no straight lines anywhere. The skin is made of thousands of panels, nearly every one a different shape.

jatiya-sangsad.blurb: Building work stopped during Bangladesh's 1971 war of independence and resumed after it. Surrounded by water, the parliament seems to float.

great-mosque-djenne.blurb: The palm-wood sticks poking out of its walls are built-in scaffolding for the yearly replastering festival. The current building dates from 1907, on a site used since the 13th century.

hallgrimskirkja.blurb: At about 75 m, it's one of the tallest structures in Iceland. A statue of the explorer Leif Erikson, a gift from the USA, stands outside.

niteroi-mac.blurb: A single central column holds up the whole saucer. The view across Guanabara Bay frames Rio's Sugarloaf Mountain.

lalibela-st-george.blurb: Legend says angels helped carve the churches by night. It's one of eleven medieval churches cut from the rock at Lalibela, and still a working church.

jewish-museum-berlin.blurb: The zigzag building has no entrance of its own: you go in through the Baroque building next door and down underground.

turning-torso.blurb: When it opened it was the tallest building in Scandinavia. The top floor is turned a full quarter turn from the bottom one.

bosco-verticale.blurb: Its trees and shrubs filter dust, absorb CO2 and shade the flats. Arborists abseil down the facade to prune them.

shwedagon-pagoda.blurb: Its tip is set with thousands of diamonds and rubies, crowned by a single 76-carat diamond. Tradition says it is more than 2,500 years old.

hassan-ii-mosque.blurb: It holds about 25,000 worshippers inside and 80,000 more on the esplanade. A laser at the top of the minaret points towards Mecca.

zeitz-mocaa.blurb: The atrium was cut out of the silo's tubes in the shape of a single grain of corn. Its pillow-shaped windows glow like lanterns at night.

cardboard-cathedral.blurb: The cardboard tubes are coated with waterproof polyurethane and fire retardant. Built as a stopgap, it was designed to last about 50 years.

yoyogi-gymnasium.blurb: It hosted swimming and diving at the 1964 Olympics and handball at the 2020 Games. Its sweeping roof hangs from two thick steel cables.
